messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: continuous-batching p95 latency spike detected for model-embed-1 in us-west-2. Error rate up, some requests timing out. Auto-escalation to eng-oncall.

erin: I got the page, digging in. seeing a sudden jump in queue length and GPU util. p95 latency jumped from ~35ms to ~1.2s across some pods.

matt: I'm taking this as primary oncall. @erin handing off — what's the latest on which services?

erin: vnode cluster cbatch-router and serve-pool-3 showing the biggest backlog. metrics: queue_length x10, microbatch sizes spiking to 32, effective batch window at 12ms (we expected ~4-6ms). KV cache miss rate up as well.

sophia: Any recent deploys to continuous-batching configs or kernel changes? I see a config rollout 30m ago that adjusted dynamic microbatch caps.

erin: yes, a hot-config rolled at 1758999900 that increased max_microbatch to 64 for throughput experiments. looks correlated.

jules: That could cause a microbatch blowup under high concurrency — larger microbatches = longer accumulation times and queueing. Also if KV cache has eviction spikes, misses cause requests to requeue.

matt: hypothesis: config increased max_microbatch -> under high concurrent traffic we formed very large microbatches -> increased tail latency -> backlog -> KV cache churn (prefix/KV cache thrashing) -> more cache misses -> extra work per request -> feedback loop.

anya: Can we mitigate quickly? options: rollback config, lower max_microbatch, disable continuous-batching, or throttle incoming concurrency per pool.

erin: I'd prefer minimal blast radius: set max_microbatch to 4 and add jitter to batching window, and roll a fast patch to reduce batch window to 3-5ms. If that fails, flip cbatch off for the cluster.

matt: Agreed. @sophia, can you push the config change to reduce max_microbatch to 4 and set batch_window_ms to 5? I'll prepare rollback steps.

sophia: On it. Patching config now.

[~10s later]
sophia: Pushed patch: 

```yaml
service: cbatch-router
max_microbatch: 4
batch_window_ms: 5
enable_jitter: true
```

sophia: Applied to serve-pool-3 (canary then all).

matt: Also add a temporary concurrency cap per-instance to 12 to avoid immediate saturation. Command: 

```bash
kubectl annotate deployment serve-pool-3 workload.redwood.io/max-concurrency="12" --overwrite
```

erin: I'm issuing a KV cache targeted flush for the affected prefix ranges to break the thrash loop. Command run: `cachectl flush --cluster serve-pool-3 --prefix-range 8-12`

jules: Good — that will evict bad entries and let cold loads repopulate in controlled way.

support-bot: Customers affected (based on errors): org-acme, org-gyro, org-bleu. Support notified, auto-ticket created.

sam: I'm posting a quick support blurb to the impacted customers: short apology, mitigation in progress, ETA ~10-20m.

[~3m later]
erin: metrics improving: queue length down ~70%, p95 latency trending back toward 80-120ms, GPU util normalized. Error rate dropping.

matt: Nice. Keep the concurrency cap and lowered microbatch in place while we monitor for 30m. If stable, plan to roll a safer variant of the previous experiment with stricter per-pod caps and more jitter.

sophia: Noted. I'll also add a guard in the rollout job to prevent max_microbatch > 8 unless rate limit low.

anya: For postmortem: root cause = config change increased allowed microbatch size without workload simulations at high concurrency + lack of circuit breaker on batch accumulation. Secondary cause = KV cache eviction sensitivity which amplified work per request.

erin: Can someone file the incident ticket and include the exact config diff / timeline? I'll attach traces and flamegraphs from the busiest pod.

jules: I'll take the postmortem write-up. We'll include recommended fixes:
- rollout safety check for microbatch caps
- runtime circuit breaker to abort forming batches past X ms
- KV cache eviction smoothing (rate-limit evictions)
- per-pool concurrency caps as a safety valve

matt: Also add an alert that triggers when microbatch median > 8 AND queue_length > 200 for >2m — both together should be a clear signal.

erin: Support update: customers acknowledged, ingested support note, no data loss, requests were slowed/failed.

sam: Support ticket updated and customers pinged with note: "We’re actively mitigating a performance regression impacting request latency; no data loss; full postmortem to follow."

[~20m later]
sophia: After 20m monitoring: stable. p95 under 200ms, error rate near baseline. removing the concurrency cap and leaving max_microbatch=4 for now.

matt: Cool. Leave temporary mitigations in place until postmortem & follow-up fixes are merged. Marked incident as "mitigated" in tracking doc.

erin: Follow-ups: create eval harness to test microbatch behavior under high concurrent synthetic load, add unit test for cache eviction smoothing, and update runbook with quick cbatch disable steps.

support-bot: Incident ticket #INC-2026-179 created, severity: P2, status: mitigated, owners: matt, erin, jules.

matt: Thanks all. Good triage and quick safe rollback. We'll do a 1:1 review tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:

jules: Adding note — keep an eye on weekend load patterns; similar bursts could trigger this if the experiment is re-enabled without guards.

matt: Closing thread, please add any lingering notes to the incident doc.
